scope: Exploratory prototype, not a replication of the original preregistration
objective: Minimize unit-cost item reviews until every declared linear target has completion-envelope width at most epsilon

gates.soundness: All exhaustive tiny-case completions lie inside reported bounds; no declared robust decision is contradicted
gates.optimality: Whenever minimum-cardinality is asserted, independent subset enumeration confirms it
gates.planner: Every output plan meets its advertised residual-width bound for every target
gates.usefulness: Report review counts and losses versus strong baselines; do not require a positive improvement to report results

limits: Candidate-derived item intervals are conditional assumptions, not calibrated truth intervals
The unrestricted [-1,1] mode is the default for unreviewed binary-score differences
No human labels, GPU generation, or population generalization are claimed
Random review baselines draw only from ambiguous items
External statistical evaluation systems optimize different objectives and are literature comparisons, not numerical baselines here
Interval arithmetic, active querying and subset-cover optimization are prior art; integration does not establish methodology novelty
